title: Kuperberg sieve for arbitrary cyclic dihedral cosets

claims.statement: For every N >= 2 and s in Z/NZ, run the general-N Kuperberg dihedral coset sieve described in proof.md, with fixed amplification and a worst-case cutoff. With n=ceil(log2 N), its total sequential work in the challenge model is O(2^(c sqrt(n))) for a fixed c>0, uniformly in N and s. Its exact growth index is 1/2, and the same configuration recovers the full secret with unconditional probability at least 2/3.

For the same general-N Kuperberg sieve and fixed configuration in proof.md, peak allocated classical space is O(2^(c sqrt(n))) bits for some fixed c>0, uniformly for every N and s, with exact growth index 1/2. This is a conservative bound by total work and includes saved labels and the sieve list.

For the same general-N Kuperberg sieve and fixed configuration in proof.md, peak allocated quantum space is O(2^(c sqrt(n))) qubits for some fixed c>0, uniformly for every N and s, with exact growth index 1/2. This is a conservative bound by total work and includes all retained coset states and work registers.

For the same general-N Kuperberg sieve and fixed configuration in proof.md, the number Q of fresh DCP source copies acquired on every execution branch is O(2^(c sqrt(n))) for some fixed c>0, uniformly for every N and s, with exact growth index 1/2. This includes all discarded samples, verification copies, and failed or restarted attempts.

For the same general-N Kuperberg sieve and fixed configuration in proof.md, the proved fractional malformed-sample tolerance is epsilon(n)=0. The guarantee assumes all acquired source copies are independent ideal DCP coset states. Under that promise the full-secret success and all four resource bounds hold jointly.

structured.error_model: Malformed fraction among acquired copies. The proved guarantee requires every copy to be an independent ideal coset state; no behavior is promised for malformed copies.
